decision.explanation: Finding 1: The only visible source is about CML and BCR-ABL TKI resistance, including imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, and ponatinib; it does not visibly address MTOR, F2108L, skin carcinoma, somatic variant origin, or serine/threonine kinase inhibitors. Citations: pmid-25349473:f01, pmid-25349473:f02. Finding 2: The visible resistance evidence is limited to BCR-ABL kinase-domain mutations, especially T315I and compound BCR-ABL mutations, in the context of BCR-ABL TKIs; this cannot be used to infer that somatic MTOR F2108L in skin carcinoma predicts resistance to a serine/threonine kinase inhibitor. Citations: pmid-25349473:f05, pmid-25349473:f06. Finding 3: The corpus therefore does not establish the supplied predictive claim as written; this is evidence insufficiency, not a demonstrated negative predictive result. Citations: pmid-25349473:f01, pmid-25349473:f02.

citations.quote: "ntolerance. Dasatinib (Sprycel(r)), a dual-Src family kinase inhibitor, and nilotinib (Tasigna(r)), a more potent BCR-ABL inhibitor, were approved for CML therapy in patients who were intolerant or nonresponsive to imatinib in 2006 and 2007, respectively. Each of these inhibitors was designed to inhibit a broader range of kinases, thereby exhibiting greater activity against a number of kinase domain mutations that could not be inhibited by imatinib.\nCurrently, newly diagnosed CML patients in the chronic phase have the option of beginning treatment on imatinib, dasatinib, or nilotinib.

A majority of patients will initially respond to one of these treatments. However, in nearly one-third of patients, first-line TKI treatment will eventually become ineffective, forcing patients to start on another TKI. Most patients will convert to either nilotinib or dasatinib. However, for some patients, especially those possessing the T315I kinase domain mutation, ponatinib (Iclusig(r)) will be the ide" . . . "L and BCR-ABL-T315I were subcutaneously injected into the right flank in female mice, and these mice were given ponatinib at doses of 10, 30, and 50 mg/kg.

Importantly, no single mutation conferring resistance was seen.\nResponses were observed for each of 15 mutations present at baseline for CP-CML patients, and 26 unique mutations in total. Response rates were similar for those with and without mutant BCR-ABL, with MCyR occurring in 56% of all patients, 49% of patients with native BCR-ABL, 64% for those with one mutation, 62% for those with two or more mutations, and 74% for those with the T315I mutant.

Though no single point mutation has shown resistance against ponatinib, compound mutations developed in 21 patients, mainly those in BC-CML or Ph+ALL. While ponatinib should still inhibit a number of compound mutants based on their in vitro cell proliferation IC50 values, a select few clinically reported compound mutants, including G250E/T315I, E255K/T315I, and E255V/T315I (IC50 values of 49 nM, 106 nM, and 425 nM, respectively), have shown increased resistance. Because these compound mutants appear only infreq" . . .
